# Jubilees Chapter 41 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Judah and Tamar; the birth of Perez and Zerah

---

**41:1** In the second year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Judah took for his son Er the daughter of Shua, who was one of the daughters of Canaan.

**41:2** Er hated his wife Tamar, for she was not one of the daughters of Canaan, and the angel of God put him to death for his wickedness.

**41:3** Judah said to his second son Onan: "Go in to your brother's wife and raise up offspring for your brother." But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his, so whenever he lay with her he let it fall on the ground.

**41:4** The LORD also put Onan to death for this wickedness.

**41:5** Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar: "Remain as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up." For he feared that Shelah might die as his brothers had died.

**41:6** Tamar went and lived as a widow in her father's house for many years.

**41:7** Judah went up to shear his sheep at Timnah. When Tamar heard that Judah had gone up, she took off her widow's garments, covered herself with a veil, wrapped herself in it, and sat by the road to Timnah.

**41:8** For she saw that Shelah had grown up but Judah had not given him to her as a husband.

**41:9** When Judah saw her he thought she was a prostitute, for her face was covered. He turned to her and said: "Let me come in to you." She said: "What will you give me to come in to me?"

**41:10** He said: "I will send you a young goat." She said: "Give me your seal and its cord and your staff."

**41:11** He gave them to her and lay with her, and she conceived by him.

**41:12** Tamar arose, went away, took off her veil, and put on her widow's garments again.

**41:13** Judah sent the young goat by his friend Hirah, but he could not find her.

**41:14** He asked the men of that place: "Where is the prostitute who sat by the road here?" They said: "There is no prostitute here."

**41:15** Judah was afraid, because what he had given her were signs against him. He said: "Let her keep them, or we will be put to shame."

**41:16** About three months later, Judah was told: "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has been immoral and is now pregnant." Judah said: "Bring her out and let her be burned."

**41:17** As she was being brought out, she sent word to Judah: "By the man to whom these belong, I am pregnant." She said: "Identify, if you please, whose seal and cord and staff these are."

**41:18** Judah recognized them and said: "She is more righteous than I, for I did not give her my son Shelah." And he did not lie with her again.

**41:19** She gave birth to twins. When one put out his hand, the midwife tied a scarlet thread on his hand. But he drew back his hand and his brother came out. She said: "What a breach you have made for yourself!" So his name was called Perez. Afterward his brother came out with the scarlet thread on his hand, and he was named Zerah.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus following LOGOS. The Judah-Tamar episode is preserved in full detail. "More righteous than I" (v.18) is Judah's famous self-condemnation. The narrative tension between Jubilees' strict intermarriage prohibition (ch.30) and Tamar's vindication here is not resolved by the text — both stand.*
